answer: Each identity registers one discharge pipe into a lagoon and locks a 70-credit bond. A sensor reads each plume in the violet band and posts it to a lagoon ledger; an auditor recomputes it and burns the bond of any pipe over its share. The lagoon has fixed capacity, so the k-th permit costs 20+4(k-1) credits: the first pays 20, the 1000th pays 4016, and 1,000 fake identities pay 2,018,000 plus 70,000 in bonds at risk. A pipe-sharing ring fails because shared flow pushes its plume over the cap, burning each bond tied to it. An honest agent pays once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
